text.p: Some 238 French tourists whose Christmas holidays in Africa were cancelled due to an air controllers strike took a travel agent and a hotel manager "hostage" in protest against their plight, French media said on Thursday.

The tourists were aboard a chartered aircraft which had to head back to France on Tuesday when it reached the half-way point of a Paris to Dakar, Senegal, flight because of an air controllers strike in much of West Africa which disrupted flights across the region, radios and newspapers said.
The frustrated travellers, who had paid for a luxury Christmas Eve dinner on an exotic West African beach, found themselves ushered instead into a dreary airport hotel outside Paris late at night.
The hotel, which had not expected the group, had sent most of its personnel home and closed its kitchen hours before and the tourists were told they would go to bed without supper.
Eyewitnesses said a near-riot ensued and the angry travellers prevented a representative of their travel agency and the hotel manager from leaving the premises until 4 a.m.

"If they were not capable of organising even a glass of milk for the children in our group, why should we have let them go home to nice Christmas dinners with their families," one irate would-be traveller told Radio France-Info on Thursday.
The "hostages" were finally released when police arrived and advised the travellers to file charges against the travel agency.
Airport authorities finally served up airline platter meals to the hungry vacationers in the middle of the night.
